normalized_proposition: The Directive concerns mutual recognition of the results of conformity tests of mass-produced telecommunications terminal equipment against common conformity specifications.
Member States are the addressees of the Directive and must implement the recognition arrangement.
Competent authorities of the Member States grant type approval, confirming that a terminal equipment type is authorised or recognised as suitable for connection to a public network.
Approved testing laboratories conduct conformity tests and issue certificates accompanied by test data and identification of the equipment and specification.
The CEPT is requested to draw up common conformity specifications in the form of NETs; CEN/CENELEC may be consulted where appropriate.
The Commission draws up annual lists and timetable, requests CEPT work, publishes lists/references and conducts the safeguard procedures.
A Committee assists the Commission, is chaired by a Commission representative, is consulted on specified matters and is serviced by a Commission secretariat.
The Council, on a proposal from the Commission, supplements and specifies the essential requirements.
Telecommunications administrations (including recognised private operating agencies) use common conformity specifications in procurement, subject to conditional waivers.
Analytic inventory of the named legal devices (specifications/NETs, tests, certificates, type approval, lists, reports, consultation, safeguard procedure) and classification of core functions.

Additional statement-level evidence propositions in Arts. 9, 11 and 12 and the recitals (Commission proposals to the Council within two years of implementation; Member State notification of national measures; addressees).
The Commission requests the CEPT to draw up common conformity specifications in the form of NETs within stated time limits.

The Commission is assisted by and consults the Committee; the Committee is chaired by a Commission representative, serviced by a Commission secretariat and may consider questions at the request of its Chairman or a Member State.
The appropriate Member State, or a body recognised by it as competent, verifies the laboratory's conformity with the CEPT accreditation system and approves it for conformity testing.
The approved laboratory carries out the tests and issues the certificate accompanied by test data and identification details.

Competent authorities of the Member States recognise the certificate of conformity for type approval and may not require further tests where the certificate relates to a common conformity specification whose references are published; recognition is without prejudice to Art. 8.
The common conformity specifications are used in all Member States by the competent authorities for any verification demanded for type approval.
Member States inform the Commission of the competent authorities and approved laboratories, send laboratory lists and regular reports, and inform the Commission of national measures.
A Member State that suspends recognition informs the Commission and the other Member States immediately, stating its reasons.

On ground (a) the Commission consults the Member States; failing agreement it seeks the opinion of an approved laboratory based outside the Member States concerned, communicates it, receives comments, and defrays the laboratory's expense; the Member State reimburses the Commission if its suspension is not maintained.

On ground (b) the Commission refers the matter to the Committee, which opines urgently; the Commission decides whether to withdraw the specification from the published list, informs the CEPT and may entrust it with a further brief.

Procurement waiver: Member States ensure administrations use common specifications; waiver (a) for replacement/transition equipment with information to the Commission and Committee; waiver (b) after market consultation with immediate notice and statement of departures, urgent Commission consultation of the Committee, a possible Commission request to the CEPT to revise, six-monthly Committee review, cessation on evidence from another Member State, and extension with Commission agreement on Committee advice.
A Member State may revoke a type approval if it considers that approved equipment does not meet essential requirements, and then applies the suspension procedures.

A Member State may, after examining the specification and test results, suspend recognition of a certificate on ground (a) (shortcomings in application) or ground (b) (specification fails essential requirements).
The Council supplements and specifies the essential requirements on a Commission proposal.
Within two years of implementation the Commission submits proposals to the Council and the Council examines them.

Qualification of the Member State's suspension procedure (reasons, consultation, laboratory or Committee assessment, recommendations, reimbursement): accountability with sufficiency indeterminate, information with a bounded reason-giving duty, or answerability.

Core conformity configuration: specification work (Commission–CEPT), testing/certification by approved laboratories, certificate recognition, national type approval, and the suspension/withdrawal safeguard form one arrangement; the question is which relations belong to it (notification/publication of authorities and laboratories; the Council's essential-requirements relation; the Commission–Committee relation).
The procurement waiver procedure is kept distinct from the conformity-assurance core (no stated coupling to the suspension/safeguard procedure).
Overlap structure: V8 records one configuration; RGAM records overlaps among the specification chain, recognition, qualification, waiver, suspension and Committee frames.

Existence of a formal architecture over the covered process: V8 asserts a bounded formal legal architecture (A01, high confidence) from K01; RGAM records an ARCHITECTURE_CANDIDATE (ARCH-01) whose I1–I3 are satisfied and whose I4 is INDETERMINATE because the constitution of NETs, of approved laboratories (accreditation system), and the electrical-safety and non-prejudice provisions rest on external instruments; RGAM asserts no architectural level (stops at S).

No whole-instrument, sector-wide or regime-level architecture is asserted: V8 defers strategy, regime and broader architecture (X01) and bounds A01 to the covered process; RGAM records the whole-instrument candidate (ARCH-02) as INDETERMINATE and 'not a forced single regime'.

Core coupling: the recognition effect of a certificate is conditional on a published reference to a specification mandated from the CEPT and is subject to suspension by Member States; national approval authority is preserved.

Whole-level property of distribution: V8 characterises the architecture as distributed conformity assurance (distribution and coupling of capacities among laboratory, national authority and Commission); RGAM records qualitative per-function allocations and leaves centralisation of the candidate undetermined with no aggregation.
Vertical distribution: Member State level (approval, suspension, revocation, waiver) and Community level (Commission, Committee, CEPT-related functions).

Discretion distribution: Member State discretion to suspend, revoke and waive (conditional); Commission discretion to consult, seek opinions, request revision and decide withdrawal; extension requires Commission agreement.
Decision competences by role: Member State (suspend, revoke), Commission (withdrawal decision, recommendations); the number of Member State decision centres is not stated.
Necessity of the Committee opinion stage before the Commission's withdrawal decision cannot be asserted because the electrical-safety branch and the non-prejudice clause rest on external provisions.

Whether the Commission's request to the CEPT is the only route by which common conformity specifications come into being cannot be asserted (NETs are regarded as equivalent without excluding other forms; NET adoption is external).
The public or private character of the CEPT is not stated in the Directive.
Depth from the rule-making position is not attributable: no legal rule links Council → Commission → CEPT → recognition as steps of a path.
No relation of ANSWERABILITY or ACCOUNTABILITY class is coded in the waiver procedure other than information relations.
The claims concern formal legal design; implementation, practice, effectiveness, laboratory independence and actual use of waivers are not asserted.

External legal dependencies as sensitivity of conclusions: the Memorandum of Understanding on NETs (Art. 2(15)), the CEPT accreditation system (Art. 2(8)), Art. 9 of Directive 73/23/EEC (Art. 8(2)) and Directive 83/189/EEC (Art. 10); claims should or should not be limited to the Directive's text.
Stopping level: V8 stops at the architectural level (A01, bounded to the covered process); RGAM stops at the subconfiguration level (highest level S; INDETERMINATE candidates).
Confidence in the architecture claim: V8 states high confidence for K01 and A01; RGAM states a provisional, INDETERMINATE outcome with I4 unresolved and unvalidated I2/I3 thresholds.

Rival groupings and boundary sensitivities for the architecture candidates: a recognition regime with specification supply as an external input; the safeguard procedure as a stand-alone procedure; the pattern explained by shared Commission/Committee participation only; several independent architectures.
Higher-order constructs: regulatory strategy, governance logic, regime membership and sector architecture.
Information flows alone do not establish accountability; accountability sufficiency is uncertain where the agent, standard or consequence is not stated.
Temporal reference: RGAM states status for the interval from adoption (1986-07-24) to repeal (1992, per neutral metadata) and notes that no application date is stated; V8 states no reference date.
Recognition is not automatic type approval: the competent authority still grants type approval.
Direction/counterparty uncertainty where the text names no actor (e.g. transmitter of lists and reports to the Committee, Art. 7(2); informing actor in Art. 7(4)(a); membership of the Committee).
